prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Move Sign-In After Adoption Selection [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +12.0%, measured +13.0% (p=0.0), won
- round 1: Redesign Waiting Screen with Interactive Tips [home, redesign]: predicted +8.0%, measured -7.6% (p=0.010995), lost: worse
- round 1: Photo Quality Guidelines on Custom Pet Upload [adoption, hint]: predicted +4.0%, measured +1.2% (p=0.763516), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Clarify Account & Pet Sync on Sign-In [sign_in, copy]: predicted +3.0%, measured -1.2% (p=0.522672), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: First Desktop Summon Hint Notification [finish, notification]: predicted +2.0%, measured -8.9% (p=0.037473), lost: worse
- round 2: Simplified Path Choice Screen Copy [choose_path, copy]: predicted +2.0%, measured +0.0% (p=1.0), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Background Waiting Desktop Notification [home, wait_info]: predicted -2.0%, measured +3.9% (p=0.122699), lost: no clear effect

Previous lessons:
Reordering the onboarding flow (moving sign-in after selection) was helpful (+13.0%).
Redesigning screens with interactive elements (waiting screen redesign) hurt performance (-7.6%).
Adding guidelines/hints (photo quality guidelines) had no clear effect.
Predictions for flow reordering were accurate (+12.0% predicted vs +13.0% measured).
Predictions were far too high for visual redesigns (+8.0% predicted vs -7.6% measured) and hints (+4.0% predicted vs no clear effect).

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Reordering the onboarding flow (moving sign-in after selection) was helpful (+13.0%).
Redesigning screens with interactive elements hurt performance (-7.6%).
Desktop hint notifications hurt performance (-8.9%), while background notifications showed no clear effect.
Copy changes and guidelines/hints showed no clear effect.
Predictions for flow reordering were accurate (+12.0% predicted vs +13.0% measured).
Predictions were consistently too high for visual redesigns, hint notifications, guidelines, and copy tweaks.
